summary.headline: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 31% to INR118 crores and PAT 37% to INR21.1 crores; order book reached INR2,000 crores.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 31% YoY to INR118 crores in Q2 FY27, with EBITDA of INR27.5 crores (23.3% margin) and PAT of INR21.1 crores. Management attributed growth to a larger order book, now INR2,000 crores including joint operations, and to consolidation of five joint operations and two subsidiaries from this year. Finance costs fell to INR3.7 crores from INR5.3 crores in the prior quarter as unsecured loans were repaid. Management expects a sharp revenue step-up in H2 as about 50% of the order book moves from design into execution during the post-monsoon season.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Q2 consolidated EPC revenue INR114 crores, up 33%; segment profit INR20 crores, up 73%. Standalone EPC revenue INR218 crores, up 26%, segment profit INR9.2 crores as stated.

segments.name: Real estate
segments.commentary: City Central Mall in Guwahati (4 lakh sq ft, 150+ brands) is almost fully operational. Division holds INR134.5 crores of assets against about INR40 crores of liabilities; management cites about 14% annual return on those assets. Rental income about INR20 crores today, targeted at INR60 crores by FY29.

segments.name: Order book mix
segments.commentary: Buildings about 31%, railways and tunnels about 25%, roads and bridges about 31%, river and slope protection about 13%. About INR900 crores executable over next 18 months; INR2,500 crores of tenders under evaluation.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin to be held at 20% or above; management declined to give specific revenue or margin numbers on the call.

Order inflow target of INR1,200 crores for FY27 and order book of about INR2,500 crores by FY28 (opening remarks). Q&A referenced a target of about INR1,500 crores over 18-20 months, with at least 70% achievement expected.
Pan-India expansion from 10 to 15 states; Odisha, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Delhi, Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh named as next.
New shopping mall plaza and residential project (4-5 phases, estimated INR500 crores value) expected to add more than INR30 crores annual rental yield from FY29.
Management expects majority of H2 revenue from projects starting from November 2026 and 'a stronger second half'.
Plans to repay the INR165 crores OCCPS in quarterly instalments of about INR60 crores a year starting June 2027, targeting full repayment within about 2.5 years.
capex_capacity: Joint venture investment of INR7.9 crores in H1 to support execution of new orders.
Common infrastructure (crusher installations, equipment procurement, branch offices) planned across high-priority states to lower costs.
Consolidation of JV borrowings from 1 April 2026 after the company obtained operational and financial control of a JV that had completed about 50% of its work.
Bank guarantees outstanding INR82.57 crores as of 30 September 2026.
demand_pricing: Order inflow: four projects worth INR317 crores in Q2, including a major bridge over River Ravi (Punjab), Turga Pumped Storage Project (West Bengal, new pumped storage segment), and AHI DMS healthcare renovation (Assam).

Bidding is restricted to technically complex projects with fewer than four to five qualified bidders; the West Bengal pumped storage win had three other qualified bidders. Management says margins outside the Northeast are similar to Northeast margins.
Government tightening of qualification criteria is reportedly disqualifying 30-40% of bidders, which management expects to lift its success rate.
Management says the company has received about INR1,200 crores of new contracts in the last 1.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why was H1 cash conversion weak relative to PAT, and what is H2 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a working capital cycle of about 90 days and reinvestment of receipts into new projects, working capital and capex; it said no fresh debt was raised and cash balances were kept low. Trade payables were reduced by INR50 crores and operating cash flow stayed positive, per the CFO remarks.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance cost fall and what debt levels are comfortable?
qa_highlights.answer: Unsecured loans were repaid and the term loan has fallen from about INR32 crores to INR12 crores, expected to be nil by FY27. Fund-based exposure is CC INR104 crores and term loan INR12 crores; the INR165 crores OCCPS is non-cash in P&L terms and repayment starts June 2027.

qa_highlights.question: How much arbitration money is due and when?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR35 crores principal (INR50 crores including interest) decided in the company's favour, of which an INR10 crore award and INR7.5 crore TDA claim were received in H1. An IPL Airport Authority project award of about INR29-30 crores is expected within 6-7 months; about INR115 crores remains pending, with INR40-50 crores expected in the next 10 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why did borrowings rise between March and September 2026?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the rise reflects consolidation of JV borrowings from 1 April 2026, after the company took over operational and financial control of a JV that had completed about 50% of its work.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the Guwahati mall unit sale dispute?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said an arbitrator was appointed over disagreement but is now suspended and discussions are ongoing on a mutual basis; no timeline was given. The units are recorded as investment property.

qa_highlights.question: Expansion beyond the Northeast and margins there?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a core share of the order book will stay in the Northeast; new wins in West Bengal and Punjab are the first outside it, with more West Bengal bids pending. It says non-NE margins are similar to NE margins.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainability of the 31% revenue growth and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 50% of the order book starts in the current month and the working season is favourable, so a sharp H2 revenue rise is expected. It plans to hold margins and does not want to trade margin for volume; it declined to give specific numeric guidance.

risks_watch: Cash conversion: H1 operating cash flow was weak relative to PAT, and the working capital cycle is about 90 days.
Arbitration recovery depends on court and department timelines; about INR115 crores is pending, including a Delhi High Court matter that may take about 2 years.
OCCPS repayment of about INR60 crores per year from June 2027 requires cash generation or refinancing.
Guwahati mall unit sale dispute has no stated resolution timeline.
Revenue ramp-up in H2 depends on execution of about 50% of the order book starting from November 2026.
Annual report for FY26 is expected in the first week of December 2026.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, order book and H2 ramp-up, but evasive on specific guidance and on the Guwahati mall dispute timeline. Cash conversion and the consolidation-driven rise in borrowings drew the most probing questions.
key_quotes: The inflection we spoke about at the close of FY26 is now showing up quarter after quarter.
So, the cash, but whatever we have generated from our business, we have reinvested into our ongoing projects.
So overall, the portfolio of projects will carry similar EBITDA margins.
So, out of the INR1,500 crores new projects that we are targeting, I personally feel we will achieve at least 70% of that.

growth.why: Management guides a stronger H2 as ~50% of the INR2,000 crore order book moves into execution from November 2026, with INR900 crores executable over 18 months and an order book target of ~INR2,500 crores by FY28, but gave no specific revenue number and the EBITDA margin floor of 20%+ is a margin rather than growth target.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management commits to hold EBITDA margin at 20% or above, but Q2 margin slipped to 23.3% from 24.7% and H1 was 22%, so no expansion is signalled.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Pan-India push from 10 to 15 states and common infrastructure (crushers, equipment, branch offices) is planned, and the new mall/residential project of about INR500 crores is planned, though no firm commissioning date is given for the mall.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Revenue grew 31% to INR118 crores in Q2 and about 50% of the INR2,000 crore order book moves into execution from November 2026, with INR900 crores executable over 18 months.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Only INR7.9 crores JV investment in H1 and a planned INR500 crore mall/residential project are disclosed, with no utilisation figure given, so a new capex announcement is conditional.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is upbeat on the H2 ramp and about INR2,500 crore order book target by FY28, but declined to give numeric revenue or margin guidance, so an upgrade is not firmly signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 operating cash flow was weak against PAT (cash conversion issue), about INR115 crore arbitration money is pending, and the INR165 crore OCCPS repayment starts June 2027 (about INR60 crore a year).

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: New pumped storage segment entered via Turga project in West Bengal and new state entries in Odisha, UP, Haryana, Delhi, Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh are guided, and the mall plaza project is planned.

rows.label: Order inflow target INR1,200 crores FY27
rows.why: Four projects worth INR317 crores won in Q2 and management cites about INR1,200 crores of new contracts in the last 1.5 years, against a FY27 inflow target of INR1,200 crores.

rows.label: Cash conversion and 90-day working capital cycle
rows.why: H1 operating cash flow was weak versus PAT of INR36.6 crores with a 90-day working capital cycle and trade payables cut by INR50 crores, so cash conversion improvement is not signalled.

rows.label: Finance cost down and term loan to nil by FY27
rows.why: Finance cost fell to INR3.69 crores from INR5.32 crores after unsecured loans were repaid, and the term loan is down from about INR32 crores to INR12 crores, expected nil by FY27.

tone.note: Management was confident on order book growth, the H2 ramp and pan-India expansion but evasive on numeric guidance and the Guwahati mall unit dispute timeline; analysts pressed on weak H1 cash conversion and the consolidation-driven rise in borrowings.
